requirements.text: An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation; no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED PCB/lamp ESA for presence of the UN R10 approval mark.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA approved as a separate component and must carry the mark.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for the circled E and the country number.
requirements.why: Defines the mandatory content of the approval mark affixed to the ESA.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for '10R-' followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.
requirements.why: Defines the mandatory content and layout of the approval mark affixed to the ESA.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall be laid out in accordance with the model in Annex 1, with dimension a = 6 mm min.
requirements.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimensions on the ESA and check a ≥ 6 mm.
requirements.why: The mark on the ESA must follow the prescribed format and minimum size.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC design (filtering, layout, grounding) and confirm the ESA passes all ESA EMC tests.
requirements.why: The LED PCB of the rear lamp is an ESA fitted to an M1 vehicle.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that the test plan and report cover radiated and conducted emission and immunity tests for the LED module.
requirements.why: The rear lamp's electronics are an ESA subject to component EMC approval.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
requirements.test_case: Perform a CISPR 25 ALSE broadband emission measurement per Annex 7 with the lamp in normal operation.
requirements.why: Sets the binding test method for the lamp ESA's broadband emissions.

requirements.text: When measured using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 6). In the 400 to 1,000 MHz band the limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.test_case: Compare the quasi-peak (or peak minus 20 dB) broadband emission spectrum from 30 to 1,000 MHz against the limit line.
requirements.why: The LED driver electronics can generate broadband emissions. [merged]

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all measured broadband readings fall below the Annex 7 limit line.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for the lamp ESA's broadband emissions.

requirements.text: The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform a CISPR 25 ALSE narrowband emission measurement with an average detector per Annex 8.
requirements.why: Sets the binding test method for the lamp ESA's narrowband emissions.

requirements.text: When measured using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband emission limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 7). In the 400 to 1,000 MHz band the limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.test_case: Compare the average-detector narrowband spectrum from 30 to 1,000 MHz against the limit line.
requirements.why: The LED driver or controller may contain oscillators that produce narrowband emissions. [merged]

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all measured narrowband readings fall below the Annex 8 limit line.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for the lamp ESA's narrowband emissions.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, shall not exceed a pulse amplitude of +75 V / -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems, or +150 V / -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
requirements.test_case: Measure switching transients on the lamp supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and check the peak amplitudes.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is supplied from the vehicle 12/24 V system and its functions are switched.

requirements.text: The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Perform ISO 11452 radiated immunity tests (ALSE, BCI, TEM, stripline or reverberation chamber) covering 20 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: The stop and position lamp functions of the ESA are immunity-related functions.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to the transient pulses conducted along 12/24 V supply lines according to ISO 7637-2: pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V) / -450 V (24 V), 500 pulses, FPSC III; pulse 2a at +37 V / +37 V, 500 pulses, FPSC I for immunity related functions (III otherwise); pulse 2b at +10 V / +20 V, 10 pulses, FPSC II (III otherwise); pulse 3a at -112 V / -150 V for 1 h, FPSC I (III otherwise); pulse 3b at +75 V / +150 V for 1 h, FPSC I (III otherwise).
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the lamp supply inputs and assess functional status.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is supplied from the vehicle 12/24 V supply lines.

requirements.text: Where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall withstand the ISO 16750-2 starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V), 10 pulses, with functional status classification B for immunity related functions (for ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases) or C (for other ESA), and D for functions not related to immunity related functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile level II ten times and classify the lamp's functional status per ISO 16750-1.
requirements.why: A rear lamp for M1 vehicles may be fitted to ICE vehicles with a starter motor.

requirements.text: Where the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and Annex 8; otherwise the narrowband limits apply.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED driver circuit for oscillators or switching regulators above 9 kHz.
requirements.why: Determines whether narrowband testing is needed for the LED PCB.

requirements.text: An ESA with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Assess whether the lamp functions (stop and position lighting) are immunity related functions.
requirements.why: Determines the applicability of radiated immunity testing to the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: An ESA that is not switched, contains no switches or does not include an inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Review the lamp circuit for switches or inductive loads to decide whether ISO 7637-2 emission testing is required.
requirements.why: Determines the applicability of transient emission testing to the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the narrowband emission test.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp with all functions (position, stop, reversing) energised at nominal voltage during the emission test.
requirements.why: Constrains the operating condition of the lamp ESA under which emission limits must be met.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand the test severity levels in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2a: Stripline 60 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); Reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity test at the Table 2a levels for the selected method and confirm compliance over at least 90 % of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.why: Sets the radiated immunity test levels the lamp's LED PCB must withstand.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2b: Stripline 50 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 62,5 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); Reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity test and confirm no frequency in 20 to 6,000 MHz falls below the Table 2b minimum levels for the selected method.
requirements.why: Sets the minimum radiated immunity level over the full band for the ESA.

requirements.text: During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" of the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Monitor the stop, position and reversing lamp functions during radiated immunity testing and confirm no degradation of light output or function.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for the lamp ESA's radiated immunity.

requirements.text: ESAs approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, in paragraph 7.
requirements.test_case: Perform CoP EMC tests on a series-production LED PCB sample against the paragraph 6 requirements and compare with the approved type.
requirements.why: The LED module PCB is an ESA; every production unit must match the approved EMC type.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified, the measured broadband and narrowband electromagnetic radiated emission levels shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits of paragraphs 6.5.2.1. (broadband: 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in 30 to 75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically, 63 dB microvolts/m in 400 to 1,000 MHz) and 6.6.2.1. (narrowband: 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in 30 to 75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically, 53 dB microvolts/m in 400 to 1,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband (Annex 7) and narrowband (Annex 8) radiated emissions of a series sample and check levels are within limit + 4 dB.
requirements.why: The production LED driver PCB emits RF disturbances and must stay within the CoP emission tolerance.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength (or BCI current) up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Perform Annex 9 radiated immunity test on a series sample at 80 % of Table 2a/2b levels and monitor lamp functions (stop, position, reversing) for degradation.
requirements.why: Production lamp electronics must keep signalling functions undisturbed under radiated fields at the CoP level.

requirements.text: When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is verified, the ESA shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions up to the conducted transient levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. (ISO 16750-2 starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b at the Table 3a/3b test levels, e.g. 12 V system: -75 V, +37 V, +10 V, -112 V, +75 V).
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses and ISO 16750-2 starting profile to a series sample on its supply lines and verify functional status classification is met.
requirements.why: Production lamp ESA is connected to vehicle supply and must withstand conducted transients without loss of stop/position lamp function.

requirements.text: When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is verified, the conducted transient emission of the ESA shall not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. (maximum pulse amplitude +75 V / -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and +150 V / -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems).
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions on the supply lines of a series sample per ISO 7637-2 and check pulse amplitudes against Table 1.
requirements.why: The production LED driver circuit switches loads and must not inject transients above the allowed amplitudes.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise stated in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic emission test of the ESA (LED modules on PCB) shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Check that the EMC test plan and report reference CISPR 25 for the ESA broadband emission test.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA and its broadband emissions are verified by this method.

requirements.text: During the broadband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp ESA with all functions (position, stop, reversing) energised at rated voltage during the emission scan and record this in the report.
requirements.why: Defines the operating state in which the ESA must meet the emission limits.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits shall apply to the ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan the ESA emissions from 30 MHz to 1,000 MHz and compare against the broadband limit.
requirements.why: Sets the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must comply with the emission limits.

requirements.text: The narrowband electromagnetic emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Check that the ESA narrowband emission test report references CISPR 25.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA and its narrowband emissions must be tested by this method.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits shall apply to the ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan radiated emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare against the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limit line.
requirements.why: Defines the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must meet the narrowband limits.

requirements.text: The ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the following radiated immunity test methods, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9: (a) absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
requirements.test_case: Review the test plan and reports to confirm the chosen method combination covers 20 to 6,000 MHz without gaps.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA whose radiated immunity must be demonstrated over the full range.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition, and shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
requirements.test_case: Operate the rear lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) during exposure and monitor for malfunction.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA must remain functional while energised in normal operation during the test.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps and dwell times according to ISO 11452-1, with test signal modulation of: (a) AM, 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz range; (b) PM2, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz range; (c) PM3, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity sweep 20–6,000 MHz with specified modulations and confirm no lamp malfunction.
requirements.why: Sets the frequency range and modulation the ESA must withstand.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply and shall limit the conducted transients it generates on the vehicle power supply.
requirements.test_case: Perform ISO 7637-2 immunity and emission tests on the lamp PCB supply lines and verify pass criteria.
requirements.why: The lamp PCB is an ESA connected to the 12/24 V vehicle supply.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b to the lamp supply and connected lines and check functional status.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is supplied from 12/24 V lines subject to transient immunity requirements.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, unless the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply lines and verify correct lamp operation.
requirements.why: The M1 rear lamp ESA is not restricted to electric vehicles, so the starting profile applies.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines and other connections operationally connected to supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 and shall comply with the applicable limits.
requirements.test_case: Measure transient conducted emissions of the lamp PCB on supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and compare with limits.
requirements.why: The lamp PCB may generate switching transients onto the vehicle supply lines.

requirements.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the ESA and confirm the approval mark is at the location given on the approval communication form and is conspicuous and accessible.
requirements.why: [recall pass]

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
requirements.test_case: Check that the ESA conducted transient immunity test report covers the ISO 16750-2 starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b per Annex 10.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The LED PCB is an ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, so its conducted transient immunity must be verified by these methods.

requirements.text: The starting profile shall be assessed according to the functional status classification defined in ISO 16750-1, and the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) of ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.
requirements.test_case: Review the test plan and report to confirm the ESA pass/fail evaluation uses the ISO 16750-1 classes for the starting profile and the ISO 7637-1 FPSC for the pulses.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This sets the pass/fail classification scheme the lamp ESA must meet under conducted transients.

requirements.text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp drawing and sample for a marking area large enough for all required markings.
requirements.why: The rear lamp is a device type-approved under R148 and must provide marking space.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually check legibility and perform a rub/durability test on the markings.
requirements.why: Applies to all markings the rear lamp carries.

requirements.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the approval mark on the lamp; it must be at least 5 mm.
requirements.why: The rear lamp carries an approval marking whose size is constrained.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and the country number.
requirements.why: Defines the mandatory content of the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number, and this sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Check the marking includes a 4-6 digit sequential number located next to the circled E.
requirements.why: Mandatory content and placement of the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4. (R1 or R2 for the rear position lamp, S1 or S2 for the stop lamp, AR for the reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Verify the presence of the correct function symbols for each lamp function in the marking.
requirements.why: The lamp contains rear position, stop and reversing functions which must be identified by symbols.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. 148R01).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '148R' followed by the series digits.
requirements.why: Mandatory content of the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: For a handed (left/right) lamp, check for a horizontal arrow in the marking.
requirements.why: A rear combination lamp is typically side-specific and must indicate its mounting position.

requirements.text: The horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of rear position lamps and in the case of reversing lamps with reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
requirements.test_case: Verify the arrow points outboard relative to the vehicle installation position.
requirements.why: The lamp incorporates a rear position lamp and a reversing lamp.

requirements.text: If applicable, to the right side of the function symbol, the additional letter "D" shall be marked on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, and the additional letter "Y" on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
requirements.test_case: If the lamp is part of an independent or interdependent lamp system, check for 'D' or 'Y' to the right of the function symbol.
requirements.why: Conditional marking for lamp functions realised as independent/interdependent systems.

requirements.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: If the lamp is approved for mounting height ≤ 750 mm with reduced distribution, check for the downward vertical arrow.
requirements.why: Rear position and stop lamps may be approved with reduced light distribution.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the presence of the approval marking.
requirements.why: Direct marking obligation on the rear lamp.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the applicant's trade name or mark.
requirements.why: Direct marking obligation on the rear lamp.

requirements.text: Lamps shall, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed and, where approved for LED substitute light source(s), the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Confirm light-source replaceability; if replaceable sources are used, check the category marking.
requirements.why: Light-source replaceability is to be confirmed; marking needed if replaceable sources are used.

requirements.text: Lamps with an electronic light source control gear and/or a variable luminous intensity control and/or a secondary operating mode and/or non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking.
requirements.why: The lamp uses PCB-mounted non-replaceable LED light sources with drive electronics.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant, the specific identification code of the module (starting letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, plus additional symbols where several non-identical modules are used, from the same applicant as the lamp mark) and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: If the LED module is replaceable, inspect it for trade name, 'MD' identification code and voltage marking.
requirements.why: The LED modules may constitute replaceable light source modules (to be confirmed).

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: If the LED module is replaceable, check the lamp for the module identification code and voltage marking.
requirements.why: Conditional lamp marking if replaceable LED modules are used.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
requirements.test_case: Verify the marking is on the lens or a part permanently attached to the lens (e.g. housing sealed to lens).
requirements.why: Constrains the location of the marking on the rear lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Check visibility of the approval marking with the lamp installed on the vehicle, opening the boot lid if necessary.
requirements.why: Constrains marking visibility for the installed rear lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that these markings are on the lamp itself.
requirements.why: Defines where the rear lamp's markings must be applied.

requirements.text: The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the light source module component.
requirements.test_case: If a replaceable module is used, verify its markings are on the module itself.
requirements.why: Conditional on replaceable LED modules being used.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: Check visibility of the single approval mark with the lamp installed on the vehicle.
requirements.why: The rear lamp groups rear position, stop, reversing lamps and retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the design to confirm no light-transmitting part (lens, retro-reflector) can be removed without removing the mark.
requirements.why: Applies to the grouped rear lamp assembly with single marking.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the single approval mark components against the minimum sizes required by R148 and R150.
requirements.why: Applies to the single mark covering the grouped lamp functions and retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' (and referenced Annexes) of UN Regulation No. 48 in force at the time of application, pertinent to each lamp (rear position, stop, reversing) and to the M1 vehicle category on which the lamp is intended to be installed, shall be applied where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Review the lamp design against the applicable UN R48 installation and individual provisions for M1 rear position, stop and reversing lamps.
requirements.why: The rear lamp is approved under R148 and must satisfy the applicable R48 provisions for M1.

requirements.text: The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Perform a vibration test on the mounted lamp, then re-check photometry, colour and aim.
requirements.why: Applies to all light-signalling lamps, including this rear lamp and its fasteners.

requirements.text: Light signalling devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated and conducted emission tests on the LED PCB / lamp assembly.
requirements.why: The lamp contains an electronic LED PCB (ESA).

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Goniometric scan of the full visibility field to confirm the maximum intensity is not exceeded.
requirements.why: Core photometric maximum for each lamp function.

requirements.text: If the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the luminous intensities measured with both lamps turned on simultaneously and the rear position lamp turned on alone shall be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by ±5° V and ±10° H of the light distribution table, with all sources in operation where a lamp contains more than one light source considered as a single lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity in the ±10° H / ±5° V field with the stop+position and position-only functions and compute the ratio.
requirements.why: The product combines rear position and stop functions.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3, with the light sources present in the lamp, and outside this field no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity across the grid for the red (position/stop) and white (reversing) functions and visually check outside the grid.
requirements.why: Colour requirements for the red and white light emitted through the outer lens.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp or stop lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as a lamp marked "D", this is permitted only for front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp configuration and approval marking: a "D" marking appears only on the rear position or stop lamp function that is built as two independent lamps.
requirements.why: The rear position and stop lamp functions are within the scope of the "D" independent-lamp provision, which governs their construction and marking.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp or stop lamp is an interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y", this is permitted only for front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp configuration and approval marking: a "Y" marking appears only on the rear position or stop lamp function that is built as an interdependent lamp system.
requirements.why: The rear position and stop lamp functions are within the scope of the "Y" interdependent-lamp provision, which governs their construction and marking.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with another function using a common light source, it shall be designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted.
requirements.test_case: Review the circuit design and measure the intensity of each function on the common light source to confirm the intensity-regulating system operates permanently.
requirements.why: The rear position lamp may share LEDs with the stop lamp, and this is the condition under which such incorporation is permitted.

requirements.text: In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source); or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the PCB LED layout for separate light sources per function, or verify the documented requirement for a vehicle failure tell-tale.
requirements.why: The product combines a rear position lamp and a stop lamp on a shared LED PCB.

requirements.text: Where a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp function, only one logo shall be incorporated and all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation shall be fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Count the logos per lamp function and repeat the photometric and colorimetric tests with the logo present.
requirements.why: This constrains the optional logo design on the outer lens and reflector of the rear position lamp.

requirements.text: Irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed as an incorporated logo.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the logo content against the vehicle manufacturer's brand statement.
requirements.why: This limits the logo content that may be designed into the lens or optics.

requirements.text: The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of the lamp in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected logo area in the direction of the reference axis and confirm it is ≤ 100 cm2.
requirements.why: This is a dimensional limit for any logo designed into the rear position lamp.

requirements.text: Stop lamps and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the stop lamp and reversing lamp apparent surfaces for the absence of a logo.
requirements.why: The product contains a stop lamp and a reversing lamp.

requirements.text: In a single lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED circuit schematic and confirm by disconnecting individual LEDs that grouped LEDs extinguish together and are treated as one light source in the failure analysis.
requirements.why: The rear position, stop and reversing lamps use multiple PCB-mounted LEDs, so their failure assessment depends on how the LEDs are grouped.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution shown in Annex 3, and the maximum intensities are not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated; or (b) a signal is produced to activate a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8., 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48. If option (b) is used, the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a failure tell-tale.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of each LED or LED group in turn and either measure the Annex 3 standard light distribution against the minimum values, with a maximum check with all LEDs lit, or verify that the failure tell-tale signal is generated.
requirements.why: The multi-LED rear position, stop and reversing lamps must meet the single-light-source failure provision.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is of category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, or the stop lamp is of category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically in case of failure of the variable intensity control.
requirements.test_case: Disable or fault the variable intensity control circuit and measure that the lamp's luminous intensity falls automatically within the steady-intensity limits of category R1 or S1.
requirements.why: This applies if the LED rear position or stop lamp uses variable intensity control (categories R2 or S2).

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp design and bill of materials to confirm the LED light sources are non-replaceable light sources or light source modules, or UN-approved replaceable light sources.
requirements.why: The lamp uses PCB-mounted LED light sources/modules, which must fall within the permitted light source types.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be designed so that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt to fit the module in other orientations or positions, and attempt to remove it without tools.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules on the PCB are replaceable light source modules.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module construction for tamper-evidence and resistance to tampering.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules on the PCB are replaceable light source modules.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall, regardless of the use of tool(s), not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to interchange the module with UN-approved light sources and with the other function modules in the housing.
requirements.why: The lamp houses several functions (position, stop and reversing), so modules with different characteristics must not be interchangeable.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Replace the module with another module bearing the same identification code and repeat the photometric measurements.
requirements.why: Ensures photometric compliance of the rear lamp functions is maintained after module replacement.

requirements.text: In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Verify the photometric and colorimetric test samples are complete lamps with the production LED PCB fitted.
requirements.why: The lamp uses PCB-mounted non-replaceable LED light sources, so compliance is assessed with its own light sources.

requirements.text: Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position or in a field of different positions, the lamp shall meet the photometric requirements for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Repeat goniophotometer measurements at each declared mounting position or at the extreme reference-axis positions.
requirements.why: Photometric compliance must hold for every declared installation orientation of the rear lamp.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the luminous intensities of the lamp functions shall be measured, and shall comply, with the light source continuously lit.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities with the LEDs in continuous (non-flashing) operation.
requirements.why: This is the operating condition under which the position, stop and reversing intensities must meet their limits.

requirements.text: The intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed to be satisfied if that requirement is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
requirements.test_case: In a disputed measurement, check each test point within ±0.25° of the nominal direction.
requirements.why: This sets the angular tolerance used to judge pass/fail of the lamp's intensity values.

requirements.text: The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of each light-signalling lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) shall be determined.
requirements.test_case: Determine and document the apparent surface outline of each function as seen along its reference axis.
requirements.why: The apparent surface of each signalling function must be defined for approval and later installation checks.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall meet the photometric requirements with a supply voltage at the lamp of 13.5 V for 12 Volt-Systems, 6.75 V for 6 Volt-Systems or 28 V for 24 Volt-Systems.
requirements.test_case: Supply the lamp at 13.5 V (12 V system) during photometric tests and verify compliance.
requirements.why: This test voltage constrains the design of the LED drive circuit.

requirements.text: Where the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp through its electronic control gear at the operating conditions declared by the applicant during tests.
requirements.why: The LED PCB may incorporate electronic drive/control gear that defines the operating conditions for compliance.

requirements.text: In the case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp at the applicant-declared operating conditions and verify photometry.
requirements.why: The lamp has non-replaceable LED light sources, whose operating conditions are applicant-specified.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5 (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Measure the HV intensity of each function on both samples and compare with the paragraph 5 minimum.
requirements.why: This is the core minimum on-axis photometric requirement for each lamp function.

requirements.text: Outside the reference axis, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5 and the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3 (Figure A3-I for the rear position and stop lamps), or not less than the intensity value in cd given in the pertinent light distribution figure (Figure A3-V for the reversing lamp), for each direction in question.
requirements.test_case: Measure at all Annex 3 grid points and compare with the percentage-derived or absolute cd minima.
requirements.why: This sets the light distribution requirement for each function.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity throughout the Annex 2 geometric visibility angles (e.g. 45°/80° or 20°/80° horizontal for rear position, 45°/45° for stop) and verify it meets the minimum.
requirements.why: This sets the geometric visibility photometric requirement for the rear position and stop lamps.

requirements.text: The lamp shall observe the provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity: within the field of light distribution the light intensity in each direction shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown on the surrounding grid lines, and for the reversing lamp no intensity measured between two directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the beam and measure between grid points where local variations appear.
requirements.why: This uniformity requirement applies to each function's light distribution.

requirements.text: Where the additional test is requested to verify visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear, the maximum intensity in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity in the 165°–180° outboard, -2.5° to +5° vertical field and verify it is ≤ 0.25 cd.
requirements.why: This limit applies to the red rear lamp functions if the optional R48 visibility verification is used.

requirements.text: The luminous intensities of the lamp functions shall comply when tested according to Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 time-dependent photometric tests for each function.
requirements.why: Annex 8 sets the time conditions under which the intensity limits must be met.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp using non-incandescent (LED) light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensities after 1 min and after 10 min of operation and check them against the min/max values.
requirements.why: The reversing lamp uses LED technology.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp and stop lamp using non-incandescent (LED) light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the position and stop lamp intensities after 1 min and after 30 min (or at stabilisation) and check them against the min/max values.
requirements.why: The rear position and stop functions use LED technology.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp (R1, steady) shall meet the requirements of Table 4: minimum luminous intensity 4∙10^0 cd; maximum luminous intensity 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp, or 8.5∙10^0 cd for a lamp marked "D"; and the standard light distribution according to Figure A3-I.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of both samples on the axis of reference and at the Figure A3-I grid points, compared against the 4 cd minimum and the 17 cd (or 8.5 cd for 'D') maximum.
requirements.why: The rear position lamp function P-01 is a steady R1 lamp (4 to 17 cd on axis), so the R1 row of Table 4 applies.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, its luminous intensity shall not exceed 6.0∙10^1 cd below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
requirements.test_case: Measure the rear position lamp luminous intensity below 5° down with the stop lamp section present and verify it does not exceed 60 cd.
requirements.why: The lamp groups the rear position and stop functions on a common LED PCB and reflector, so the reciprocal-incorporation limit may apply.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1, the rear position lamp (R1) shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer check over the full Table A2-1 field of geometric visibility, verifying at least 0.05 cd everywhere.
requirements.why: The geometric visibility intensity requirement of Table 4 applies to the R1 rear position lamp.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Simulate LED and light-source failures and verify the failure behaviour required by paragraph 4.6.
requirements.why: The lamp uses multiple LED light sources, so the failure provisions referenced by this paragraph apply.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the emitted light through the outer lens and verify they fall within the red boundaries.
requirements.why: The rear position lamp emits light through the red PMMA lens, and its colour is prescribed as red.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd and shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60∙10^2 cd for a single lamp (1.30∙10^2 cd for a lamp marked "D").
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of both samples at the specified test points; check the minimum and maximum against Table 7.
requirements.why: x

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall meet the requirements in Table 10: minimum luminous intensity 8.0∙10^1 cd; maximum luminous intensity 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the H-plane, 6.00∙10^2 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D, and 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D; standard light distribution according to Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples at the Figure A3-V test points, checking minimum and maximum values per zone.
requirements.why: Product includes a reversing lamp (P-03) of category AR whose photometry is set by Table 10.

requirements.text: Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices and its photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied at that angle.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at 30° inwards and verify it is at least 25 cd.
requirements.why: Applies if the reversing lamp is approved for paired installation only, constraining its inboard light distribution.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the reversing lamp's emitted light through the outer lens window and check they fall within the white limits.
requirements.why: Reversing lamp (P-03) emitting through the outer lens must be white, despite the red-tinted lens elsewhere.

requirements.text: The lamps (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp) shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under this Regulation, with compliance with the requirements set forth in paragraph 5 verified as follows.
requirements.test_case: Compare production samples against the approved type documentation and re-test the paragraph 5 requirements on random production lamps.
requirements.why: The rear lamp is type-approved under R148, so series production must match the approved type.

requirements.text: The lamps shall comply with the minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 4.
requirements.test_case: Audit the CoP control plan for periodic photometric and colorimetric testing of random production lamps per Annex 4.
requirements.why: The CoP control requirements apply to every R148-approved lamp type produced.

requirements.text: The lamps shall comply with the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 5.
requirements.test_case: Have production lamps sampled per the Annex 5 scheme (samples A/B) and verify they pass the deviation criteria.
requirements.why: Production lamps of the approved rear lamp are subject to inspector sampling under Annex 5.

requirements.text: When production lamps are checked for conformity of production, no measured photometric value of the rear position lamp, stop lamp or reversing lamp shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity of production lamps at the Annex 3 test points and check that no value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent.
requirements.why: This CoP photometric tolerance applies to all the lamp functions of the product.

requirements.text: For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to Table 12. For a required minimum of 7∙10^-1 cd: 5∙10^-1 cd (20 %) / 3∙10^-1 cd (30 %). For 6∙10^-1 cd: 4∙10^-1 cd / 2∙10^-1 cd. For 3∙10^-1 cd: 2∙10^-1 cd / 1∙10^-1 cd. For 7∙10^-2 cd: 5∙10^-2 cd / 3∙10^-2 cd. For 5∙10^-2 cd: 3∙10^-2 cd / 2∙10^-2 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity in the geometric visibility fields of Annexes 2 and 3 on production lamps and compare with the Table 12 equivalent values.
requirements.why: The rear position and stop lamps have minimum-intensity requirements throughout their visibility fields, and these are checked at CoP against Table 12.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall meet the minimum angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1: horizontal 45° inboard / 80° outboard (20° inboard / 80° outboard, used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm); vertical 15° above / 15° below (15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above / 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm).
requirements.test_case: Goniometer check that the rear position lamp's apparent surface remains visible and meets the minimum intensity across the stated horizontal and vertical angles for the intended mounting height.
requirements.why: The product incorporates a rear position lamp, whose geometric visibility row in Table A2-1 applies.

requirements.text: The angles of geometric visibility shall be applied as shown for lamps to be mounted on the right side of the vehicle, mirrored for lamps mounted on the left side, with inboard and outboard directions referenced to the lamp's mounting side.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the visibility test set-up orients the inboard/outboard angles according to the lamp's left or right mounting side.
requirements.why: Defines how the inboard/outboard visibility angles apply to the left- or right-hand rear lamp variant.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp or the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, its photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the downward photometric verification to 5° if it is ≤ 750 mm.
requirements.why: This test condition constrains the photometric verification of the product's rear position and stop lamps.

requirements.text: Unless specified otherwise, the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall, for the various directions of measurement, meet the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, the H = 0° and V = 0° direction corresponding to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference, with values mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at each grid point relative to the reference axis, comparing against the required percentage of the minimum intensity.
requirements.why: Defines the angular photometric minimums that each fitted signalling lamp function must achieve.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light pattern of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall be substantially uniform, i.e. the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.
requirements.test_case: Scan intensity between grid points and verify that each value is at least the lowest minimum of the surrounding grid lines.
requirements.why: Imposes a uniformity requirement between the measured grid directions for the lamp functions.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp, if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the lit reversing lamp; where local variations are seen, measure intensity between adjacent measurement directions and confirm ≥50 % of the lower prescribed minimum.
requirements.why: Specific local-uniformity limit applying to the reversing lamp function present in the product.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall emit, in the various directions of measurement, at least the minimum intensities given by the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, expressed as a percentage of the minimum intensity required for rear position lamps in the corresponding table.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at each Figure A3-I grid point, comparing against the stated percentage of the required minimum intensity for the rear position lamp.
requirements.why: The product includes a rear position lamp (P-01), which is covered by the Figure A3-I standard light distribution.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (category S1, S2 or MS) shall emit, in the various directions of measurement, at least the minimum intensities given by the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, expressed as a percentage of the minimum intensity required in Table 7 (S1/S2: 6.0∙10^1 cd; MS: 4.0∙10^1 cd).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the stop lamp at each Figure A3-I grid point, verifying at least the stated percentage of the Table 7 minimum.
requirements.why: The product includes a stop lamp (P-02) of category S1/S2/MS, which uses the Figure A3-I distribution.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall emit, at each measuring point of Figure A3-V (expressed in degrees from the axis of reference), at least the minimum luminous intensity in cd given in Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the reversing lamp at all Figure A3-V points, checking that each value meets or exceeds the cd minimum.
requirements.why: The product includes a reversing lamp (P-03), whose minimum light distribution is set by Figure A3-V.

requirements.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, the mass-produced rear lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Dimensionally inspect production samples against the approved type drawings and check deviations stay within manufacturing tolerances.
requirements.why: CoP mechanical/geometric conformity applies to every production lamp of the approved type.

requirements.text: With respect to photometric performances, any mass-produced rear position, stop and reversing lamp chosen at random shall meet the photometric requirements when tested according to paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of a randomly selected production lamp per paragraph 4.8 and comparison with the required values.
requirements.why: Photometric CoP of the LED signalling functions is checked on randomly selected production lamps.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Spectroradiometric measurement of colour inside the Annex 3 light distribution field on production samples with the non-replaceable LEDs fitted.
requirements.why: Colour of emitted light is a CoP criterion for each production lamp.

requirements.text: Conformity of production of the lamp shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
requirements.test_case: Verify the production control plan includes periodic photometric and colorimetric tests of each lamp function.
requirements.why: Defines the product characteristics that must be maintained and verified in production.

requirements.text: The sampled lamp shall meet the minimum photometric values at the points listed in Annex 3 for each function (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) and the required chromaticity coordinates.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at each Annex 3 grid point and chromaticity on sampled production lamps and confirm all minima and colour limits are met.
requirements.why: Sets the measured pass criteria the production lamp must satisfy.

requirements.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution shall additionally comply at the points in time of Table A8-1: rear position lamp 4 s after switch ON (reference coordinate HV); stop lamp 0.2 s after switch ON (reference coordinate HV); reversing lamp 0.2 s after switch ON (reference coordinate HV).
requirements.test_case: Measure the HV intensity at the specified time after switch ON for each function and scale the distribution by the HV ratio to check compliance.
requirements.why: These run-up time points apply to the product's rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions.

requirements.text: Where a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, it is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the functions use LED technology only and that the paragraph 1.2 measurements are compliant.
requirements.why: The lamp functions use LED light sources, so their time-point compliance relies on the paragraph 1.2 results.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the lamp (function) shall meet the corresponding minimum intensity requirements at all points in time, starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 (4 s for rear position, 0.2 s for stop and reversing) and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Record intensity continuously from the Table A8-1 time until photometric stability, and check it never falls below the minimum values.
requirements.why: LED drive electronics may show unexpected run-up behaviour, which would make the lamp subject to the continuous minimum-intensity check.

requirements.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Inspect any external control gear of the LED lamp for its identification number and manufacturer name.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The LED lamp may use an external electronic control gear that would need its own marking.

requirements.text: If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: Check the design for lens detachability; if detachable, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The lamp has a separate outer lens sealed to the housing, so the marking location depends on whether the lens is detachable.

requirements.text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the main body of each device sharing the outer lens and confirm it carries only the marking of its own functions.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The outer lens covers several functions (position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector), which may be approved as separate devices.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to insert the light source in all possible orientations and confirm that only the correct position is achievable.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Binds the lamp design if any function uses replaceable approved light sources; LED replaceability is still to be confirmed.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, applying the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed.
requirements.test_case: Gauge the holder dimensions against the relevant IEC 60061 holder data sheet.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a holder construction requirement on the lamp when replaceable approved light sources are used.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the light source holder shall also conform to the IEC 60061 holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Gauge the holder against the IEC 60061 holder data sheet for the prescribed LED substitute category.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This adds a holder conformity condition when LED substitute light sources are prescribed for the lamp.

requirements.text: Where a variable intensity control is used, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp through the full range of variable intensity control signals and verify that the measured intensities stay within the paragraph 5 range.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies to the stop/rear position lamp functions if they are driven at variable intensity.

requirements.text: Where a variable intensity control is used, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp: (a) under night-time conditions, for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions; (b) under standard conditions (good visibility, MOR > 2,000 m, and clean lens), for other systems.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity under night-time or standard-condition control signals and compare it with the steady maximum in paragraph 5.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Limits the maximum intensity of the variable-intensity stop/rear position lamp functions.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall comply with the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at the grid points of Figure A3-I, compared against the required percentages of the minimum on-axis intensity.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The stop lamp P-02 is the S1 category for M1, and its light distribution must follow the Table 7 row for S1.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1, the category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 3∙10^-1 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at the boundary directions of the Table A2-1 geometric visibility field and verify each value is ≥ 0.3 cd.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is the minimum intensity across the visibility field that applies to the stop lamp function present on the product.

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of LED light sources and check the lamp behaviour against paragraph 4.6.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The LED stop lamp must meet the failure provisions stated for the stop lamp function.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the emitted light and verify they fall within the red boundaries.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The colour requirement applies directly to the stop lamp's emitted light through the red outer lens.

requirements.text: Where the reversing lamp type approval is granted applying the condition of verification only up to 30° inwards, the reversing lamp shall only be installed on a vehicle in a pair of devices.
requirements.test_case: Check the communication form (item 9.1.3) and the vehicle installation drawings to confirm that the lamp is fitted only as a pair.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The approval condition restricts how the AR lamp may be installed on the M1 vehicle.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector (device belonging to an approved type) shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the retro-reflector drawing and sample for a marking area large enough for the UI or approval marking plus the 'TOP' marking.
requirements.why: The rear lamp incorporates a retro-reflector approved under R150, which must provide marking space.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually check legibility and perform a rub/indelibility check on the markings.
requirements.why: Applies to all markings carried by the retro-reflective device.

requirements.text: The approval marking on the retro-reflector shall be sized according to the value 'a' defined in Table 1, i.e. minimum a = 5 mm for a retro-reflector for motor vehicles of Class IA (independent) or Class IB (combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight).
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension 'a' of the approval marking on the sample and confirm it is at least 5 mm.
requirements.why: The M1 rear retro-reflector is Class IA or IB, for which Table 1 sets the minimum marking size.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled 'E' and the country number.
requirements.why: This is the content of the approval marking the retro-reflector must carry.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4- to 6-digit sequential approval number.
requirements.why: This is a required element of the approval marking on the device.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the marking layout that the sequential number is adjacent to the circled 'E'.
requirements.why: This is a positional constraint on the marking of the device.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5. ('IA' for an independent retro-reflector, 'IB' for one combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the correct class symbol, IA or IB.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector's class symbol must appear in its approval marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. 150R01).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '150R' followed by the two-digit series of amendments.
requirements.why: This is a required element of the approval marking on the device.

requirements.text: Where the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
requirements.test_case: If a UI is used, compare the marking layout with Figure I.
requirements.why: This is a format constraint on the marking if the UI option is chosen for the device.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the device for the applicant's trade name or mark.
requirements.why: This is a mandatory marking on the retro-reflective device.

requirements.text: In the case of a retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, the retro-reflector shall bear the word 'TOP' inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the retro-reflector is rotation-sensitive and, if so, verify that a horizontal 'TOP' marking appears at the top of the illuminating surface.
requirements.why: The lamp's retro-reflector is Class IA/IB and may need an orientation marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraph 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the assembled device to confirm all markings are legible.
requirements.why: This is a location and legibility constraint on the device markings.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (rear lamp incorporating the retro-reflector), the marking shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: Install the lamp on the vehicle or a representative fixture and verify the single approval mark is visible.
requirements.why: The rear lamp groups or combines the retro-reflector with other lamps and may use a single mark.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed, no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
